title: Retire an asset — controlled transition with lifecycle/audit records
objective: Verify POST /assets/:uuid/retire moves an eligible asset to Retired status with reason, records lifecycle + audit events atomically, and retired assets are excluded from assignment/maintenance actions.
preconditions: Operator+/Manager session per transition rules; asset in an eligible status (e.g., In Stock/Available, no open blockers).
test_data: asset RT-1; retire payload {reason 'End of life'}; Idempotency-Key
steps: POST /api/v1/assets/<RT-1>/retire with reason + Idempotency-Key.
Verify status transition and response shape.
Attempt to assign RT-1 after retirement → expect 409.
Verify history/audit entries for the retirement.
expected_result: 200 with asset in Retired status; lifecycle + audit events with actor/timestamp/reason; subsequent assign/reserve/maintenance-create rejected with stable 409 code; role gating per transition rules (employee/auditor → 403).

title: Disposal blockers enforced — 409 DISPOSAL_BLOCKED lists every blocker
objective: Verify POST /assets/:uuid/dispose is rejected with 409 DISPOSAL_BLOCKED enumerating blockers when the asset has an open assignment, open maintenance record, active reservation, in-transit transfer, or pending approval.
preconditions: Assets each carrying one blocker class (assigned; open maintenance; active reservation; in-transit; pending approval once approvals exist).
test_data: dispose payload {method <disposal method uuid>, reason 'Salvage'} per blocked asset
steps: POST /assets/<blocked-uuid>/dispose for each blocker class.
Record status, error code, and blocker list contents.
Clear the blocker (return asset / complete maintenance / cancel reservation) and retry → expect success.
expected_result: Each blocked attempt → 409 DISPOSAL_BLOCKED with the full list of current blockers (user-safe, no over-disclosure); no partial state change (status unchanged, no disposal dates set); after clearing blockers, disposal succeeds; all attempts audited per policy.

title: Dispose asset — terminal state, method/reason/proceeds recorded, non-reusable
objective: Verify successful disposal records disposal date, method, reason, and (finance-gated) proceeds; disposed assets are terminal by default and cannot be assigned/transferred/edited into reuse.
preconditions: Retired (or eligible) asset with no blockers; disposal methods seeded; manager session with finance.view; operator session without.
steps: POST /assets/<uuid>/dispose as manager.
Verify response + asset fields (disposal date/method/reason, status disposed).
Verify proceeds visible to finance-capable roles and hidden from operator.
Attempt assign/transfer/reserve/retire again/PATCH-to-in-stock on the disposed asset.
expected_result: Disposal persisted with method+reason+date; proceeds finance-gated; status disposed is terminal — all reuse attempts rejected 409 with stable codes; lifecycle + audit events complete.

title: Disposal with blockers — authorized exception path (if enabled)
objective: Verify the documented authorized-exception behavior: only the designated elevated role may dispose despite blockers (when the feature is enabled by config), with mandatory recorded justification; otherwise confirm no bypass exists.
preconditions: Asset with an open blocker; users: elevated role (per config, e.g., system_admin), regular manager.
test_data: dispose payload with justification text; config flag state recorded
steps: As regular manager, attempt dispose with justification → expect 409 DISPOSAL_BLOCKED (no bypass).
As elevated role, attempt dispose with justification; record outcome.
If exception succeeded: verify justification stored + audited; if rejected: verify documented 'no exception in v1' behavior.
expected_result: Behavior matches the documented configuration: exception only for the elevated role with recorded justification (immutable audit), or uniform blocking. Regular roles never bypass BR-006.

title: Reopen disposed asset — elevated permission + recorded justification, history preserved
objective: Verify POST /assets/:uuid/reopen requires elevated permission and a recorded justification, appends (never erases) lifecycle history, and returns the asset to a documented non-disposed status.
preconditions: Disposed asset; manager (non-elevated) and elevated-role sessions.
test_data: reopen payload {justification 'Disposed in error — asset recovered from supplier'}; Idempotency-Key
steps: Attempt reopen as manager without justification → expect 400/403.
Attempt reopen as manager with justification → expect 403 (not elevated).
Reopen as elevated role with justification → verify success + resulting status.
Verify history shows retire→dispose→reopen chain with all events intact.
expected_result: Justification mandatory (400 without it); non-elevated → 403; elevated reopen succeeds to documented status; original disposal record preserved (BR-003); audit events capture actor + justification; replay with same Idempotency-Key does not double-apply.

title: Disposed assets searchable to authorized users, hidden/scoped appropriately
objective: Verify disposed assets remain findable via search/list filters (status=disposed) for authorized roles within scope, and remain invisible across scopes (404) — non-reusable but auditable.
preconditions: Disposed asset in dept A; admin, dept-A deptmgr, dept-B deptmgr sessions.
steps: As admin: filter list by disposed status → asset present.
As dept-A deptmgr: same filter → asset present.
As dept-B deptmgr: list + direct detail access → absent / 404.
expected_result: Disposed assets discoverable by authorized in-scope users with correct status badge semantics; scope hiding intact (ADR-007 404); counts in dashboard/report aggregates consistent with the same rule.

title: Disposal requiring approval — pending until decided (integration with FR-024)
objective: Verify that when the disposal transition rule requires approval, dispose creates a pending ApprovalRequest instead of executing, and the disposal executes only on approval (rejection leaves asset unchanged).
preconditions: Transition rule with requires_approval for disposal enabled (seed/config); requester + approver users.
test_data: dispose request by manager; approve by deptmgr/admin; second case rejected
steps: POST dispose → verify 202/pending response with approval reference; asset NOT yet disposed.
Approve via /approvals/:uuid/approve → verify disposal executes (status disposed, events linked).
Repeat with reject → verify asset unchanged and approval recorded as rejected.
expected_result: Approval-gated disposal follows pending→executed/rejected flow; no disposal before decision; full correlation between approval and lifecycle/audit events; requester cannot approve own request (separation of duties when enabled).

title: E2E Journey J-5 — retire and dispose of an asset
objective: UI journey: retire an asset, attempt disposal with a blocker (verify blocked dialog lists blockers), clear blocker, dispose with method+reason, verify terminal badge + history; approval step included when enabled.
preconditions: Full stack seeded; Playwright; manager + approver credentials.
test_data: eligible asset; one blocked asset (open assignment); disposal method
steps: Open asset detail → retire action; confirm dialog names asset + consequence; submit; verify Retired badge.
On blocked asset: attempt dispose; verify blocker list rendered non-destructively.
Clear the blocker; dispose with method + reason; verify terminal Disposed badge and disabled actions.
Open history; verify retire/dispose chain; screenshots as evidence.
expected_result: Journey matches API truth at each step; destructive confirmations per §8.5; no optimistic success; blocked state explained; evidence captured. (If browser runner still unavailable: BLOCKED with justification.)
